Name: Requiring the landmarks preservation commission to create a public records online portal.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring the landmarks preservation commission to create a public records online portal

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Land Use
This Introduction was Re-referred to Committee by Council to the Committee on Technology

Summary: This bill would require the Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC), in collaboration with other relevant City agencies or offices, to create and maintain a publicly accessible online portal that makes available certain public records, materials, and other information maintained or received by the LPC on or after January 1, 2016, including those relating to public hearings and public meetings, landmark designations, and LPC permits.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring the landmarks preservation commission to create a public records online portal

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Chapter 3 of title 25 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 25-323 to read as follows:
§ 25-323 Public records online portal. a. The commission, in collaboration with the department of information technology and telecommunications and any other relevant agency or office, shall create and maintain on the commission’s website a publicly accessible online portal that makes available all public records, materials, and other information maintained or received by the commission on or after January 1, 2016, in relation to:
1. All public hearings and public meetings, including all testimony and evidence received at such public hearings and public meetings conducted by the commission; 
2. All designations and proposed designations of landmarks and historic districts; 
3. All permit applications filed with, and all permits issued by, the commission; and
4. All violations issued, and all violations rescinded, by the commission.  
b. Any such public records, materials, or other information maintained or received by the commission on or after the effective date of the local law that added this section, shall be made available as soon as practical on the online portal created pursuant to subdivision a of this section.  
§ 2. This local law takes effect 180 days after it becomes law.
